segments.flavor: the drop that says the station name
segments.text:
Zane: Voltage FM. Where the sunrise is a rumor and nobody has confirmed it yet.
Zane: [shouting] Hands up. Back to the floor.

segments.flavor: the sign-on that never signs off
segments.text: Zane: This is Voltage FM. The night never ended. You just blinked for nine hours. Music.

segments.flavor: peak time is a permanent condition
segments.text:
Zane: Voltage FM. Every hour here is peak time, including the ones with daylight in them.
Zane: The bass is structural. The floor is legal. Go.

segments.flavor: the lights never came up
segments.text:
Zane: You are on Voltage FM, where the lights never came up and nobody asked them to.
Zane: [cheerful] Stay loud. Here comes the low end.

segments.flavor: Zane's one more speech, delivered like a manifesto, while Mara counts them against him
segments.text:
Zane: One more. That is the whole philosophy of this station. One more is a promise, not a number.
Zane: Numbers end. Promises just keep playing. Here is the next one.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system Zane personally wired; Mara reports the BPM
segments.text:
Zane: That low end came through a rig I wired myself, with a torch in my teeth.
Zane: Two cables were wrong. Both of them improved it. More of that now.

segments.flavor: Mara identifies the last track with an invented label, catalogue number and BPM; Zane pretends he knew
segments.text:
Zane: Knew that one. Voltage Black, catalogue oh four two, one hundred twenty-four beats per minute.
Zane: Mara left the sleeve face up on the desk. I have excellent eyes. Onward.

segments.flavor: Rollo calls from a taxi that is still not there; the driver has an opinion on the setlist
segments.text:
Zane: Rollo, where are you?
Rollo: Three streets out. The driver says your last track was too fast for a Tuesday.
Mara: Tell him Tuesday is not a tempo. Zane, take it faster.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a club product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Mara
segments.text:
Zane: Second Wind chewing gum, for the hour after your last hour. One piece, one more hour.
Mara: Second Wind may cause honesty, dancing at work, and a strong opinion about hi-hats.
Zane: Chew one, hear the difference, and let this next record do the rest.

segments.flavor: Zane's one more speech, delivered like a manifesto, while Mara counts them against him
segments.text:
Zane: That was one more. This is one more. I contain an unlimited supply of one mores.
Mara: That is eleven one mores since midnight. The word has stopped meaning anything at all.
Zane: Words are cheap, records are expensive, and here comes a very costly number twelve.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system Zane personally wired; Mara reports the BPM
segments.text:
Zane: That whole record came through a rig I built from spare parts and stubbornness.
Mara: One hundred twenty-six beats per minute, and the left speaker is a converted fridge.
Zane: That fridge holds a note longer than anything I have ever paid money for. More.

segments.flavor: Mara identifies the last track with an invented label, catalogue number and BPM; Zane pretends he knew
segments.text:
Mara: That was Halogen Duchess on Grey Ceiling, catalogue G C oh nine, one hundred thirty.
Zane: Grey Ceiling. Obviously. I have had that one since before it had a catalogue number.
Mara: You asked me what it was. Twice. In writing. Next one, please.

segments.flavor: Rollo calls from a taxi that is still not there; the driver has an opinion on the setlist
segments.text:
Zane: Rollo is on the line. Rollo, tell me you can see the door from there.
Rollo: I can see a door. The driver says it is the wrong one and he is not turning.
Mara: He has been not turning for forty minutes. That is commitment. That is almost a genre.
Zane: Stay on the meter, Rollo. We will play you in.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a club product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Mara
segments.text:
Zane: The smoke machine is running again and nobody in this building admits to owning it.
Mara: So the makers of Nobody's Fog have sent us one of their own. Sincerely, apparently.
Zane: Nobody's Fog. Atmosphere with no paperwork. It belongs to no one and follows everyone.
Mara: Nobody's Fog is not a fire. Please stop calling. Back into the deep end.

segments.flavor: Zane's one more speech, delivered like a manifesto, while Mara counts them against him
segments.text:
Zane: Here is the thing about one more. One more is not a quantity, it is a posture.
Mara: It is absolutely a quantity. I keep a notebook, and the notebook disagrees with your posture.
Zane: Burn the notebook. Nobody in history ever left a club early because of good bookkeeping.
Mara: Fourteen. That is fourteen. Play your one more, manifesto man.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system Zane personally wired; Mara reports the BPM
segments.text:
Zane: I ran the cable for that sound through the ceiling, on a chair, in the dark.
Mara: One hundred twenty-two beats per minute, and the chair is still up there, holding it.
Zane: The chair is part of the system now. It is in the signal path.
Mara: Then the chair gets a credit on the next white label. Roll the next one.

segments.flavor: Mara identifies the last track with an invented label, catalogue number and BPM; Zane pretends he knew
segments.text:
Mara: Track ID. Salt Cathedral, on my own white label, Third Shift, catalogue T S three.
Zane: Third Shift. I knew that. I said that. I said it in my head, very loudly.
Mara: One hundred eighteen beats per minute. Fifty copies pressed. Forty-nine are in my flat.
Zane: Fifty copies. That is not a label, that is a hobby with a catalogue number.
Mara: It is a hobby that you have now played twice. Here comes the third time.

segments.flavor: Rollo calls from a taxi that is still not there; the driver has an opinion on the setlist
segments.text:
Zane: Rollo, give me a distance. Any distance. A number of streets, a country, anything.
Rollo: Close. The driver has a disc in the glovebox and he would like it played.
Mara: Everyone has a disc in the glovebox. That is why the roads are so slow.
Zane: What is on it?
Rollo: He says it is the sound of a real night. Eleven minutes. No drums.
Mara: No drums. Tell him the meter and the kick drum both keep time. Next record.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a club product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Mara
segments.text:
Zane: Brought to you by Dawn Patrol, the only sunglasses engineered for people leaving at sunrise.
Mara: The lenses are so dark that they are, technically, a small wall.
Zane: Dawn Patrol. Because daylight is an opinion, and you do not have to agree with it.
Mara: They also float, which matters to nobody, and is printed on the box anyway.
Zane: Float sunglasses. Wear them indoors. Live a full and heavily shaded life.
Mara: Dawn Patrol protects against nothing. Not daylight, not regret. Straight back to the floor.

segments.flavor: Zane's one more speech, delivered like a manifesto, while Mara counts them against him
segments.text:
Zane: [serious] One more is a unit of time. It is longer than an hour and shorter than regret.
Mara: Science has not confirmed this. My stopwatch has. Your one more averages forty-one minutes.
Zane: Forty-one minutes is a fair one. A short one more is an insult to the floor.
Mara: You said that at the last one more. And the one before that one more.
Zane: Consistency is the whole brand. One more, starting now. Watch the clock, Mara.
Mara: Watch started. Nobody believe him. Take it away.

segments.flavor: back-announce the mix as the sound system Zane personally wired; Mara reports the BPM
segments.text:
Zane: Channel three on this desk does not work, and I have never once fixed it.
Mara: You wired channel three yourself, with a lighter and a paperclip.
Zane: I did. That is why I respect it. It failed honestly, on its own terms.
Mara: It has been failing honestly for nine years. That is a long, honest career.
Zane: Everything here came out of one long night and one warm lighter.
Mara: And it is holding one hundred twenty-nine beats per minute without a single wobble.
Zane: Steady as a heart, built by a man with no sleep.
Mara: Do not touch channel three. Do not look at channel three.
Zane: Nobody touches channel three. Everybody dances. That is the arrangement. Let it run.

segments.flavor: Mara identifies the last track with an invented label, catalogue number and BPM; Zane pretends he knew
segments.text:
Mara: Track ID. Copper Ankle, on Blue Hour Industries, catalogue B H one one, promo only.
Zane: Blue Hour. I was in the room when they cut that. Great biscuits.
Mara: Blue Hour Industries is a garage with no door and one working plug.
Zane: That is the room. I stood by the plug. I remember the plug clearly.
Mara: One hundred thirty-one beats per minute. Two hundred copies. One hundred ninety went nowhere.
Zane: Nowhere is a strong market. Nowhere has taste and very cheap rent.
Mara: You had never heard of this record before I put it on the desk.
Zane: I had heard of it spiritually. Play it again and I will remember more.
Mara: I will play the other side. You can invent a memory of that one too.

segments.flavor: Rollo calls from a taxi that is still not there; the driver has an opinion on the setlist
segments.text:
Zane: Rollo. I can hear an engine. I can hear it going around in a circle.
Rollo: Roundabout. Fourth lap. The driver refuses to leave while this record is still playing.
Mara: That is the correct decision. Nobody should exit a roundabout during a breakdown.
Zane: Rollo, how much is on the meter?
Rollo: The driver has turned the meter off. He says this one is on him.
Mara: [gasp] A free lap. The man has become a fan. Print him a card.
Zane: Two more laps, Rollo. Tell him the next one is longer and better.
Rollo: He says he can do six laps. He has nowhere to be either.
Mara: Nobody here has anywhere to be. Six laps, Zane. Give the man his record.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a club product, sincere announcer grammar, rapid disclaimer from Mara
segments.text:
Zane: This next part is sponsored by Still Going, the app for the hour after the hour.
Mara: You open it and it shows you a map of everyone who has not gone home.
Zane: Little glowing dots. Each dot is a person saying, not yet, not yet, not yet.
Mara: The dots move very slowly. Some dots have stopped moving. Still Going does not check.
Zane: Still Going. Find the room that is still warm. Follow a dot. Become a dot.
Mara: Still Going cannot find your coat, your keys, or the reason you left the house.
Zane: None of those things are the point. The point is the next room.
Mara: The next room is right here. Turn it up.

segments.flavor: Ear Cathedral earplugs
segments.text:
Zane: Voltage FM is brought to you tonight by Ear Cathedral, the earplug with a nave.
Mara: It is shaped like a tiny church. It sits in the ear and hums.
Zane: Ear Cathedral removes the hiss and keeps the holy part. Hear tomorrow, from inside tonight.
Mara: Ear Cathedral is not a place of worship and cannot marry you. Back to it.

segments.flavor: Puddle, the droppable water bottle
segments.text:
Zane: Here is a word about Puddle, the only water bottle designed to be dropped repeatedly.
Mara: It bounces. It also holds its shape after a stranger stands on it twice.
Zane: Puddle. Because hydration should survive the same night you did. Cap included, cap optional.
Mara: Puddle is not a flotation device, a weapon, or a friend. Music, please.

segments.flavor: Floorproof trainers
segments.text:
Zane: Floorproof trainers are engineered for eight hours of standing, one hour of nonsense, and a very long walk home.
Zane: Floorproof. Your feet will forgive you eventually, and nobody else will. Straight back into this one now.

segments.flavor: Nine Volt energy shot
segments.text:
Zane: The next hour is powered by Nine Volt, the energy shot with a warning on both sides.
Mara: One bottle. Two flavours. Copper, and a second flavour they refuse to name.
Zane: Nine Volt goes in cold and comes out as confidence. Your hands will find rhythm.
Mara: Your hands will find rhythm and then keep it for two days.
Zane: Nine Volt. Feel the current. Recommended by nobody, loved by everybody on this floor.
Mara: Nine Volt is not tested, approved, or sorry. Do not blink. Here we go.

segments.flavor: Arrival, the car service that is nearly there
segments.text:
Zane: Arrival is the car service that promises to be nearly there, and it always keeps that exact promise.
Zane: Arrival. You will be nearly there forever, in total comfort. Here is some music to travel by.

segments.flavor: Neverclose, the all-night laundry
segments.text:
Zane: A sincere word about Neverclose, the laundry that has no closing time and no staff.
Mara: The machines run all night. The lights buzz. It smells like a warm cloud.
Zane: Bring the shirt. Bring the whole night. Neverclose takes both and returns one of them.
Mara: Neverclose is not responsible for items, colours, or anything you leave behind. Back in.

segments.flavor: Softfloor bass underlay
segments.text:
Zane: Tonight's next record is presented by Softfloor, the underlay that keeps your bass entirely yours.
Mara: Two centimetres of grey foam standing between a good night and a formal letter.
Zane: Softfloor absorbs the low end before it reaches the ceiling of the person below.
Mara: The person below will still know. They always know. But they cannot prove it.
Zane: Softfloor. Structural concerns, solved quietly. Roll it out and turn it up.
Mara: Softfloor is not soundproofing and will not survive a tribunal. Let the bass through.

segments.flavor: The Long Yolk, breakfast for the undefeated
segments.text:
Zane: The Long Yolk serves a full, quiet breakfast to people who have not yet agreed that it is morning.
Zane: The Long Yolk. Eggs, silence, and absolutely no questions at all. Until sunrise, stay exactly where you are.

segments.flavor: the White Label Hour
segments.text:
Mara: It is time for the White Label Hour, where I play a record with no information.
Zane: No artist. No title. No catalogue number. Just a blank sleeve and a promise.
Mara: This one has a thumbprint on the label. That is the only fact available.
Zane: Whose thumb?
Mara: Unknown. Possibly the pressing plant. Possibly a person who regretted the whole thing immediately.
Zane: I love a regret record. Regret is the most danceable emotion we have.
Mara: Four minutes long. Nobody will ever identify it. Nobody will ever hear it again.
Zane: Then this is the only time it exists. White Label Hour. Let it go.

segments.flavor: the Smoke Report
segments.text:
Zane: Time for the Smoke Report. Mara, what are we looking at on the floor?
Mara: Visibility is down to one metre. Heavy fog from the machine that nobody owns.
Zane: Conditions?
Mara: Warm, damp, faintly sweet. A front is moving in from the cloakroom corner.
Zane: Any chance of clearing?
Mara: None. The machine has no switch. We looked. We looked for a long time.
Zane: Then the forecast is more of the same, with a strong chance of bass.
Mara: Smoke Report complete. Visibility poor, morale excellent. Straight into the next one.

segments.flavor: BPM Court
segments.text:
Mara: BPM Court is now in session. I am the judge. Zane is the accused.
Zane: I plead not guilty and also I would like to leave.
Mara: The charge is playing a one hundred forty beat per minute record at the wrong moment.
Zane: The moment was right. The room was wrong. That is a different crime.
Mara: Three people sat down. One person left. One person applauded, which confuses the case.
Zane: That one person understood the assignment. I would like them named in the record.
Mara: The court finds you guilty of enthusiasm in the first degree. Sentence is immediate.
Zane: What is the sentence?
Mara: You play the same record again, and this time the room sits down properly.
Zane: Court is adjourned. Here it comes, faster than before.

segments.flavor: the Lost Property Table
segments.text:
Zane: Tonight on the Lost Property Table, we have four items and no explanations.
Mara: One glove. One single trainer. A door key with a bell on it.
Zane: A bell. Somebody attached a bell to their key so they could hear it fall.
Mara: They heard it fall. They kept dancing. That is a decision made with full information.
Zane: And item four?
Mara: A sandwich, wrapped, untouched, labelled with a name I will not read out.
Zane: Somebody packed a sandwich for the club. That is the most optimistic object here.
Mara: The table stays by the door until sunrise. Claim nothing. Dance more.

segments.flavor: the Sunrise Denial
segments.text:
Zane: It is time for the Sunrise Denial, the hourly moment where I deny the sunrise.
Mara: The sky outside is doing something orange and it is doing it very confidently.
Zane: That is a streetlight with ambition. Denied.
Mara: Birds, Zane. There are birds.
Zane: Birds work nights too. Some birds are simply committed. Denied.
Mara: Noted. The denial stands. The sun has no comment.
Zane: The night continues by official ruling. Play something with no daylight in it.

segments.flavor: the cloakroom ticket nobody claims
segments.text:
Zane: Cloakroom ticket forty-one has been on the hook for three weeks now.
Mara: A long black coat. Heavy. One pocket contains a receipt and a single screw.
Zane: A screw. Loose in the pocket. That is a person who fixes things reluctantly.
Mara: Or a person who removed a screw from something and walked away forever.
Zane: Both stories are good. Neither one comes back for the coat.
Mara: Forty-one stays on the hook. The coat has become part of the building.
Zane: Everything stays here eventually. Coats, people, the smoke. Let us keep going.

segments.flavor: the Catalogue Reading
segments.text:
Mara: Time for the Catalogue Reading. I read catalogue numbers aloud and Zane stays completely quiet.
Zane: I will try. I have never managed it.
Mara: K R two one. Deep Hollow four. Night Trade oh oh six.
Zane: Night Trade oh oh six is the greatest record ever pressed and I am emotional.
Mara: You lasted nine seconds. That is a personal best by a wide margin.
Zane: Read the last one properly and I will play it immediately.
Mara: Night Trade oh oh six. Go on then. Play it.

segments.flavor: the Rig Tour
segments.text:
Zane: Welcome to the Rig Tour. Tonight we meet the subwoofer. His name is The Landlord.
Mara: You named a speaker after the man who writes you letters about that speaker.
Zane: I did. Respect your enemy. Keep him in the corner where you can see him.
Mara: The Landlord weighs ninety kilograms and moves two centimetres to the left every night.
Zane: He is walking. Slowly. Towards the door. He wants out and I understand him.
Mara: One day you will open up and The Landlord will simply be gone.
Zane: Then I will follow the marks on the floor and bring him home.
Mara: That is the Rig Tour. Say goodnight to The Landlord. He is about to speak.
